finalText:
I found and fixed a real defect I had reported as green last cycle. Correcting that first.

**`npm test` was failing about two runs in five**, and had been since this run added the fifth fixture. My previous report said the suite was green; it was green on the runs I happened to observe, and I did not re-run it enough times to see the flake. The one occurrence I did see earlier in the session I dismissed as transient without diagnosing it. That was wrong.

The cause is not in the product. `test/fixtures/build.mjs` removed each fixture directory and immediately recreated it under the same name; on the overlay filesystem these builds run on, the name then resolves, `existsSync` and `statSync` both confirm it, `chdir` into it succeeds, and the child's startup `getcwd()` returns ENOENT — so every `git init` failed with `fatal: unable to get current working directory`. Reproduced outside the project: remove-then-recreate fails within 35 rebuilds of one path. WP1 never saw it because it had one fixture and one rebuild per run; eight fixtures made it a coin toss.

Renaming the old directory aside before recreating fixes it:

```
before   node test/fixtures/build.mjs   2 failures in 5 runs
after    node test/fixtures/build.mjs   0 failures in 25 runs
         npm test                       0 failures in 8 runs
```

`git()` in the builder also retries that one stderr string up to four times, then gives up loudly. It is a **backstop, not the fix** — with it disabled the suite still passed 6 of 6 — but a 120-rebuild stress loop tripped the residual once, and I would rather not leave a builder that fails one run in twenty. It is safe to retry because it means git never started, so it is not an answer about a repository. Nothing under `src/` retries anything.

The regression test rebuilds a probe fixture 60 times through `buildCase` — the real path — and checks each rebuild produces both branches. On a filesystem without the quirk it passes without proving anything, and the comment says so.

## Final state

```
npm run typecheck → clean
npm run build     → dist/ + examples/basic.html
npm test          → 99 tests, 99 pass, 0 fail  (8 consecutive runs)
npm run size      → 11114 bytes, 4139 gzipped (target 30720, hard limit 51200)
```

Eleven commits on `uf/visualmerge-c18570bd208d-1-53822343`, working tree clean. Everything else stands as reported: the six red-then-green trap commits, the complete §2.5 mapping against reproduced output, `unsupported[]` and its taxonomy, the exit-code discipline, `--allow-unrelated-histories`, `up-to-date`/`fast-forward`, eight fixtures, and the frozen contract at `schemaVersion: 1` with `typechange` as its single WP2 addition.

Still deliberately left alone: the unwritable-ODB message, the clean-typechange row wording (WP5's), docs excluded from the long-git-message scan, and no `HUMAN GATE` ticked.
